item.title: Reading Unreliable Narration
item.description: Compare what a fictional narrator claims about a family’s decision to sell their house with what readers can infer from shifts in viewpoint, gaps in the story, and details the narrator overlooks.

children.definition: A teller whose sincere version of events proves inaccurate because of limits in memory, knowledge, or judgment.
children.example: Elena is a fallible narrator who sincerely remembers her sister voting for the sale, although the minutes record that her sister was absent.
children.translation_uz: xotirasi, bilimi yoki mulohazasidagi xatolar sabab voqealarni beixtiyor notoʻgʻri bayon qiladigan hikoyachi
collocations: the testimony of a fallible narrator

children.definition: The filtering of fictional events through a particular viewpoint, which determines whose perceptions and knowledge are available to the reader.
children.example: The chapter’s focalization through Elena’s sister lets readers see the buyer’s signature before Elena enters the room.

children.definition: The telling of events from a point in time after they occurred.
children.example: Through retrospective narration, Elena calls the dinner a farewell, although at the time she thought the family was simply gathering to discuss repairs.
collocations: a novel told through retrospective narration

children.definition: A technique in which third-person prose takes on a figure’s idiom or judgments without quoting their words or explicitly reporting their thoughts.
children.example: The prose slips into free indirect discourse after Elena's sister asks for more time: Another week to think it over? Her sister would be asking the house for its consent next.
children.translation_uz: erkin bilvosita nutq, yaʼni qahramonning fikri yoki ohangi hikoya bayoniga singgan nutq
collocations: a passage in free indirect discourse
a shift into free indirect discourse

children.definition: Existing within the fictional world and therefore potentially accessible to the people who inhabit it.
children.example: The ticking Elena mistakes for footsteps is diegetic, coming from the hall clock her sister winds before the buyer arrives.

children.definition: A departure from the current point in a story to present an episode that occurred earlier in its chronology.
children.example: The sale dinner is interrupted by an analepsis in which Elena promises her mother that she will never sell the house without her sister’s consent.
children.translation_ru: аналепсис, возврат к более раннему эпизоду повествования

children.definition: The degree of psychological closeness that the manner of telling creates between the reader and a person whose experience is depicted.
children.example: The narrative distance narrows during the signing as the prose moves from describing Elena’s steady hand to registering her fear that the pen will slip.
children.translation_uz: bayonda oʻquvchining qahramon kechinmalariga qanchalik yaqinlashtirilishi

children.definition: An attempt to clear oneself of blame by presenting one’s actions, motives, or circumstances in a favourable light.
children.example: Elena’s insistence that she ‘only passed the papers around’ reads as self-exculpation once her sister reveals who arranged the sale.

children.definition: A significant gap in a text or testimony where material the reader has reason to expect is missing.
children.example: There is a lacuna in Elena’s version of the dinner where her sister’s reply should be, immediately before Elena declares that everyone agreed.

children.definition: Advance awareness given to readers of an outcome that the people depicted have yet to discover.
children.example: The opening chapter depicts the buyer taking possession of the house. That piece of readerly foreknowledge changes how we interpret the sisters' later dispute over whether to sell.
children.translation_ru: заблаговременное знание читателя об исходе событий

children.definition: Material such as a title, preface, or epigraph that accompanies the main text and shapes how readers approach it.
children.example: The novel’s paratext includes a dedication to ‘those whose consent was assumed’, casting doubt on Elena’s claim before she makes it.

children.definition: A clash between the meanings or values that different viewpoints attach to the same event.
children.example: The perspectival incongruity is clearest at the signing, which Elena calls a gesture of solidarity and her sister regards as an act of betrayal.
children.translation_ru: расхождение в трактовках или оценках одного и того же события с разных точек зрения
children.translation_uz: bir voqeani turlicha talqin qilish yoki unga turlicha baho berishdan kelib chiqadigan ziddiyat

children.definition: A person within one level of a story who takes over the telling of a further story contained within it.
children.example: The buyer becomes an embedded narrator when he tells Elena’s niece how he negotiated the sale privately with Elena.
children.translation_uz: asosiy hikoya ichida alohida hikoyani aytib beruvchi shaxs
collocations: the voice of an embedded narrator

children.definition: The enclosing storyline that establishes the circumstances in which one or more inner stories are told or encountered.
children.example: In the outer narrative, Elena’s niece finds the family’s recording years after the sale and plays it to find out why the sisters stopped speaking.
children.translation_uz: ichki hikoya qaysi vaziyatda aytilishi yoki unga qanday duch kelinishini koʻrsatuvchi asosiy hikoya
